label: D1
title: Contexts and authorizations
math:
c \;::=\; \mathsf{call}(C, f, \vec v) \;\mid\; \mathsf{create}(w)
\\
a = (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)
reading: A request is the list of calls an entry approves, with the rule named for each, the signers, the ledger and the generation.
text: A context is one call or contract creation in an authorization entry's invocation tree. An authorization \(a\) carries the entry's contexts \(\vec c = c_1, \dots, c_n\) in preorder, root first; one rule index \(j_i\) per context; the claimed signers \(S\); the ledger \(\ell\); and the account's grant generation \(g\).

label: D2
title: Rules and *allows*
math:
\mathit{allows}(r, c, S) \iff \mathit{sc}_r(c) \land \bigwedge_{\varphi \in \Phi_r} \varphi(c)
\\
\qquad\qquad \land\ k_r \le |\Sigma_r \cap S|
\\
\mathit{allows}(R, c, S) \iff \exists r \in R.\ \mathit{allows}(r, c, S)
\\
R' \sqsubseteq R \iff \forall c, S.\ \mathit{allows}(R', c, S)
\\
\qquad\qquad \implies \mathit{allows}(R, c, S)
reading: A rule allows a call when it names that contract and function, every argument condition holds, and enough of its signers signed.
text: A rule \(r\) has a scope \(\mathit{sc}_r\) (one contract and a function list; false on creations), argument conditions \(\Phi_r\), signers \(\Sigma_r\) and a threshold \(k_r\) over distinct signers, and optionally a cap \((\lambda_r, P_r)\), a last ledger \(u_r\) and a generation \(g_r\). *allows* reads none of the last three; *authorize* checks them. A rule set allows what one of its rules allows; \(R' \sqsubseteq R\) when \(R\) allows, under the same signers, everything \(R'\) allows.

label: D3
title: *authorize* and runs
math:
\mathit{authorize}(R, \rho, (\vec c, \vec j, S, \ell, g)) = \rho' \iff
\\
\quad |\vec j| = |\vec c| \land |\rho| = |R|
\\
\quad \land\ \forall i.\ j_i < |R| \land \ell \le u_{r_i} \land g_{r_i} \in \{\bot, g\}
\\
\qquad\qquad \land\ \mathit{allows}(r_i, c_i, S)
\\
\quad \land\ \forall s \in S.\ \exists i.\ s \in \Sigma_{r_i}
\\
\quad \land\ \rho' = \mathit{charge}(\cdots \mathit{charge}(\rho, c_1, j_1) \cdots, c_n, j_n)
reading: *authorize* accepts a request only if each named rule is live and allows its call, every signer belongs to a named rule, and every charge fits.
text: Here \(r_i = R_{j_i}\). \(\mathit{charge}(\rho, c, j)\) leaves \(\rho\) unchanged when \(R_j\) has no cap; otherwise it reads the amount \(c\) carries, refusing a call that carries none, and applies Definition 4's check to rule \(j\)'s record. Each charge must succeed. *authorize* returns the next records or the first refusal, and a refusal changes nothing. A run applies authorizations in order, keeping the records on a refused one.

label: D4
title: Window, check and *spent*
math:
\mathit{inWindow}_P(L, t) \iff \max(0,\, L - P) < t \le L
\\
\mathit{check}_{\lambda, P}(h, \ell, x) = h' \;\land\; x > 0 \implies
\\
\qquad \sum_{k:\ \mathit{inWindow}_P(\ell,\, t_k)} y_k \;+\; x \;\le\; \lambda
\\
\qquad \land\ h' = ((t_k, y_k))_{k:\ \mathit{inWindow}_P(\ell,\, t_k)}
\\
\qquad\qquad \cdot\, (\ell, x)
reading: The window at ledger L holds the charges made after L − P and through L; a new charge must fit under the limit.
text: A record is a list \(h = ((t_k, y_k))_{k=1}^{m}\) of positive charges in ledger order, its total their sum. The check of a charge \(x\) at ledger \(\ell\) refuses \(x < 0\); accepts \(x = 0\), leaving \(h\); and otherwise refuses a ledger before the newest charge, an overflow, {{fact:evaluator-history-bound}} entries already kept, or a window total above \(\lambda\). On acceptance it keeps the entries in the window at \(\ell\) and appends \((\ell, x)\). \(\mathit{spent}_j(R, \rho, \vec a)\) lists \((\ell_a, x)\) for each positive charge that the accepted authorizations of run \(\vec a\) make to rule \(j\), in order.

label: D5
title: Derivation
reading: A derived grant comes from its parent by zero or more of the ten attenuation steps.
text: \(\sigma\) is one of rule-core's ten attenuation steps: drop a rule; remove functions, or restrict functions; add an argument condition; remove signers, or raise a threshold; add a cap, lower its limit, or lengthen its period; set or lower the last ledger. No step changes a rule's target or generation. \(\mathit{attenuateAll}(R, \vec\sigma) = R'\) applies a list of steps and implies \(\mathit{Derives}(R, R')\).

label: D6
title: Documents and lowering
reading: A grant document is lowered into stored rules under the account's address, excluded set and current generation, or refused.
text: For a document \(d\) on account \(A\), \(\mathit{Doc.allows}(d, A, c, S)\) holds when some rule of \(d\) covers \(c\)'s contract and function, its argument constraints hold and its principals are signed by \(S\); no rule allows a creation. \(\mathit{Doc.Valid}(d)\) holds when every rule that requires all its signers names distinct signers, fewer than \(2^{32}\) of them, and no rule has a not-after ledger of 0. \(\mathit{lower}(d, A)\) is the rules of an account document, followed by the recovery rule when \(d\) configures recovery. With \(X = \mathit{excluded}(d_s, A)\) for the account document \(d_s\), which is \(A\), the adopted controller and, if configured, the zero-knowledge adapter and pool, \(\mathit{lowerScoped}(d, A, X, g)\) refuses a document that configures recovery or has a rule whose target is \(A\), a member of \(X\) or the account's self-administration, and otherwise lowers \(d\)'s rules stamped with generation \(g\). Document conditions lower to rule-core's {{fact:rule-core-conditions}} as {{ref:tab:tab-attenuation}} says; a cap adds the upper bound of the largest `i128` on argument 2, a type guard.

label: D7
title: Account events
math:
\mathsf{applyDoc}(d'):\ (A, d_s, g) \mapsto (A, d', g)
\\
\mathsf{completeRecovery}(t):
\\
\quad (A, d_s, g) \mapsto (A, t, g + 1) \quad (g < 2^{64} - 1)
\\
\mathit{issue}((A, d_s, g), d)
\\
\quad = \mathit{lowerScoped}(d, A, \mathit{excluded}(d_s, A), g)
reading: Applying a document keeps the generation; a completed recovery advances it by one.
text: An account state \(s = (A, d_s, g)\) is the account's address, its account document and its grant generation. \(\mathsf{applyDoc}(d')\) replaces the account document; \(\mathsf{completeRecovery}(t)\) installs the recovery target \(t\) and advances the generation, and is refused when \(g\) is the largest `u64`. A refused event leaves the state unchanged. \(\mathit{run}(s, \vec e)\) applies events in order, and \(\mathit{completions}(s, \vec e)\) counts the completed recoveries among them. A grant document \(d\) is *issued* in \(s\) by lowering it under the account's address, the excluded set of its account document and its generation.

label: D8
title: Host run
reading: A model of the Soroban host running one transaction under enforcing authorization.
text: A model of soroban-env-host running a transaction of contract calls under enforcing authorization. Every call is a frame that a failure rolls back. `require_auth` of an address holds when the frame's direct caller is that address (invoker authority), or when an authorization entry of the address matches; on its first match the address's `__check_auth` runs on the entry's contexts in preorder, then the expiration is checked and the nonce consumed. Stellar-account signers, `require_auth` inside `__check_auth`, `require_auth_for_args`, `authorize_as_current_contract`, contract creation as a call and source-account credentials are outside the model.

label: D9
title: Denotation
math: \forall x.\ \exists y.\ f_{\mathrm{T}}(x) = \mathsf{ok}(y) \land \llbracket y \rrbracket = f(\llbracket x \rrbracket)
reading: Denotation maps the translation's values to the model's, so the two can be compared.
text: \(\llbracket \cdot \rrbracket\) maps the translation's values (byte vectors, `u32` and `u64` scalars, rules, caps, records, contexts, signers and outcomes) to the model's. A translated function \(f_{\mathrm{T}}\) agrees with its model \(f\) when, for every input, it succeeds and its result denotes the model's result on the denoted input. {{ref:stmt:total-equivalence-of-the-evaluator}} and {{ref:stmt:lowering-equivalence}} are stated this way.
